Por último, el patrón acentual es yámbico del tipo ligero-pesado. [p. 146] Los ejemplos compuestos que he mostrado en la tabla (3.39) nos sirven también para develar el patrón yámbico del zapoteco de San Agustin Mixtepec. El patrón acentual de esta lengua, por lo tanto, corresponde a un sistema yámbico del tipo ligero - pesado (CVµ CVµµ).
new_statements.translation: [p. 57] the lexicon of the language is built mainly of monosyllables and, since the correlate of stress is prosodic weight, these monosyllables must obligatorily be bimoraic. Finally, the stress pattern is iambic, of the light-heavy type. [p. 146] The compound examples shown in table (3.39) also serve to reveal the iambic pattern of San Agustín Mixtepec Zapotec. The stress pattern of this language therefore corresponds to an iambic system of the light-heavy type (CVµ CVµµ).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lexical words are basically monosyllabic and every stressed syllable must be bimoraic (vowel lengthening or moraic fortis coda). When a word has two syllables (root-root compounds, disyllabic Spanish loans) the stress falls on the final syllable, which is heavy, while the first syllable is a light monomoraic 'ill-formed foot': an iambic light-heavy (CVµ CVµµ) pattern, i.e. right-edge stress of the phonological word.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned for SAMZ. (Beam de Azcona's 2016 slides on the related San Bartolomé Loxicha Miahuatec float '¿acento secundario?' for the first root of compounds, with clitics extrametrical.)
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the first member of a compound and the initial syllable of loans (e.g. [ko.ne:x] 'conejo', [Barto:l] 'Bartolo') lose their bimoraicity, which is the evidence for the pattern. Enclitics are not discussed in the SAMZ metrical section.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (ω): monosyllabic roots in isolation, root-root compounds and disyllabic loanwords; analysis in a moraic/foot framework, duration (not pitch) as the correlate of stress. Data: Beam de Azcona's 2002-2005 field recordings of the last fluent speakers plus the author's 2016 notes.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding source is titled 'Fonología del miahuateco' but its chapter 3 is a separate synchronic phonology of San Agustín Mixtepec Zapotec (sana1286, ISO ztm) built on Beam de Azcona's 2002-2005 recordings of the town's last fluent speakers plus the author's 2016 fieldwork; chapters 4 and 5 treat Santo Domingo de Morelos (loxi1235/ztp) and San Bartolo Yautepec (sanb1242 area) and are not used here. Beam de Azcona 2004 reports only two fluent speakers in 2003-2004, so the description is of a moribund variety. The San Bartolomé Loxicha stress statement (final syllable of the lexical word, clitics extrametrical) in Beam de Azcona 2016 belongs to sanb1241, not to this language.

sources.note: pp. 165-166 'El sistema suprasegmental de San Agustín Mixtepec': 3 tones (alto, bajo, ascendente), simple/cortada/quebrada syllables, limited length contrast; no statement of where stress falls. p. 168 (Miahuatec, SBarL data): unstressed syllables = first members of compounds and enclitics, with no contrastive tone. Historical remarks on loss of post-tonic vowels in Southern Zapotec.
